transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but... honestly, what made me come in is that I feel like the warm part of me just sort of shut off recently. 

Like, after my shift at work, I'll sit on the couch with my husband or try to watch my regular shows, and... well, I know I *should* feel comfort, or even just a little happy to be home and relaxing, you know? But there’s just nothing there right now. I feel terrible even admitting that out loud, because he's so sweet and I know I should be happy. Does that make sense? I just hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you noticed a change in how you feel about activities you used to enjoy, like watching your regular shows or spending time with your husband?

Yeah, exactly... um, I mean, I still do them. I still sit there with him and watch the TV, so it's not like I'm completely falling apart or anything. I definitely don't want to make it sound worse than it is. 

It's just... that little spark or that cozy feeling I usually get is kind of missing right now. I still love spending time with him, I really do, I promise. It's just harder to actually *feel* the joy in it at the moment, if that makes sense. Is that... is that something you hear a lot? I just feel so guilty even complaining about it when I have a good life, you know?
Have you noticed feeling down or having a low mood most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Um... no, not really. I wouldn't say I feel down or depressed all day, definitely not. I mean, I still get up and go to work and do my job, you know? I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around crying all the time, because I'm really not. 

It's more just... that blank feeling I was talking about. Like I'm just going through the motions. But I wouldn't call it a low mood, really. Just... flat, maybe? I hope that's the right way to describe it. Does that sound like what you were asking about, or did I misunderstand?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you normally like?

Um, well, I guess I kind of touched on that a second ago, right? With the TV shows and sitting with my husband? 

But, um, other than that... I don't think so? I mean, I still try to do things I normally do. I don't want to be someone who just gives up on everything, you know? So I still go to work, I still try to keep the house nice... I think I'm still doing okay with all of that. I'm not, like, completely losing interest in my whole life or anything dramatic. 

I just... I don't know, maybe I'm just a little tired lately? Is it okay if I don't really have a good answer for that one? I'm sorry, I hope I'm being helpful.
Can you think of any activity or moment recently that truly brought you joy or made you feel genuinely happy, even for a little while?

Um... I've been trying to think about that, actually. I really have. And, um... I don't want to sound ungrateful, because my husband is so wonderful and he tries so hard to cheer me up. 

But... honestly, that's kind of the main reason I decided to come in and talk to you. I just feel like... like the warm part of me just sort of shut off? Like, I'll be sitting there with him, or trying to watch my favorite shows after my shift at the warehouse, and in my head, I know I *should* feel comforted, or at least a little bit happy. But... there's just nothing there. It's just blank. 

I'm really trying, though, I promise. I don't want to be like this. Is it... is it bad that I can't think of a time I felt genuinely happy recently? I hope I'm not making things sound worse than they are, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way, with the lack of joy or that 'blank' feeling you described?

Um, well... I guess it's been about three weeks now? 

I really don't want you to think I'm just letting myself go or not trying to bounce back, because I really am. But... yeah, it started right around three weeks ago. That was when, um... well, there was an accident at the warehouse where I work. A pallet collapsed, and my coworker got hurt pretty badly. 

I mean, I wasn't the one who got hurt, so I know I shouldn't be making a big deal out of it or anything. I just... I think that's when this whole blank feeling started. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not overreacting by still feeling this way after three weeks. Is that... is that a normal amount of time to feel a little off after something like that?
Can you tell me if you're still able to feel pleasure or enjoyment in any activities, even small things, or does everything feel the same to you emotionally?

Um, I think... well, I kind of mentioned this a minute ago, but... yeah, it's pretty much everything feeling the same. Just... blank. 

I really hope I'm not sounding like a broken record, but that's honestly the main reason I decided I needed to come talk to you. I just feel like that warm part of me completely shut off. Like, I'll be sitting on the couch with my husband, or trying to watch one of my favorite shows after my shift, and I know in my head that I *should* be feeling comfort, or at least a little spark of enjoyment, you know? But... there's just nothing there right now. 

I'm really trying to find the good in things, I promise I am. I don't want to be a downer for my husband or anyone else. But even the small things just kind of feel... flat. Is it okay that I'm struggling to find pleasure in things right now? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Can you tell me if there’s been any moment, even something small, where you’ve felt even a little bit of pleasure or happiness in the past three weeks?

Um... I really wish I could say yes, because I know I should be looking for the bright spots, you know? I really have been trying to notice little things. Like, my husband brought me my favorite coffee the other morning, and I smiled and told him thank you, and I meant it... but inside, it just felt... I don't know, like I was just going through the motions. 

I haven't really felt that actual spark of happiness. It's just been that same flat feeling since the accident. I hope that doesn't make me sound completely hopeless or like I'm not trying hard enough to get better. I really am trying. Is it normal to just not feel anything at all for this long? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the kind of progress you're looking for.
Have you noticed a decrease in your energy level or felt more fatigued than usual, even when you're not doing anything physically demanding?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I've been any more tired than usual. 

I really hope that's a good sign? Like, maybe I'm doing okay physically, even if my emotions are a little stuck right now. I still go to work and do my shifts, and I try to keep up with things around the house so my husband doesn't have to do it all. I don't want to be a burden or anything. 

So, yeah, my energy feels pretty normal, I think. I haven't noticed feeling extra fatigued or anything like that. Is that... is that what you'd expect to hear? I just want to make sure I'm answering right.

Can you tell me if you’ve completely stopped enjoying all activities, even things you used to find pleasurable, or if there are still some things that you look forward to, even if you don’t feel the same level of enjoyment?

Um, I know I'm kind of repeating myself, and I'm really sorry if I'm not explaining it very well... I do try to look forward to things, I really do. I don't want to sound ungrateful or anything. But... yeah, it's like I was saying earlier. That warm part of me just feels completely shut off right now. 

Even with the things I used to love, like sitting with my husband or putting on my shows after a long shift at the store... I sit there and I know I should be feeling comfort, or even just a little bit happy, but... there's just nothing there. It's honestly what made me come in to see you in the first place. I'm really trying to get back to normal, though. I hope it's okay that I don't have a better answer for you yet? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the truth.

Um, yeah, I guess... I guess it really is just like I was saying before. I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably sounding like a broken record here, and I don't mean to waste your time. 

I definitely still have that part of me that *knows* I should be enjoying things. Like, I haven't forgotten how much I love my husband or how nice it is to relax after work. I really try to focus on that, you know? I tell myself, "You like this, this is good." But the actual feeling of it... the pleasure part... it's just not connecting right now. 

I'm really trying, though, I promise. I don't want you to think I've just given up or that I'm not putting in the effort to get better. Is it... is it okay that I'm still struggling with this? I hope I'm making sense.

Um, I... I know you just asked me about this, and I feel terrible making you repeat yourself. I really hope I'm not being difficult. 

But, um, no, I wouldn't say I've completely stopped having interest in *everything*. I still go to work, and I still care about making sure my husband has a nice dinner, and I want to keep the house clean. I really do still care about those things, and I want to do them well. 

It's just the... the actual feeling of enjoying it that's missing right now. But I haven't lost interest in trying, I promise. I'm still trying really hard to do all the things I'm supposed to do.
